newsitem.title: USA: Rumors Brazil buying Argentine wheat no surprise.
newsitem.headline: Rumors Brazil buying Argentine wheat no surprise.

text.p: U.S. exporters could not confirm market talk that Brazil was seeking 500,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat for February/March delivery, although several exporters did not rule out the possibility of such a purchase.
"It would be pretty hard to get any confirmation today (Tuesday) because of the (New Year's) holiday. But I would not be surprised if it gets done," one U.S. exporter said.
Wheat futures on the Chicago Board of Trade and the Kansas City Board of Trade firmed in abbreviated holiday sessions, supported partly by the Brazilian rumors.

Brazil has bought wheat from neighboring Argentina in the past. "That is pretty traditional business for both of those countries. It is not a big surprise. We knew that they still had some business to get done," he added.
"Argentina had such a huge crop this year," a second U.S. exporter said. "It would be easier for them to export it right across the border to Brazil" than to ship it farther away.
On December 19, Argentina raised its 1996/97 wheat harvest forecast to 15.2 million tonnes from 14.9 million tonnes, Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola said.
Another determining factor was price. The exporter quoted Argentine wheat at around $140 a tonne FOB for February/March delivery compared with about $170.00 a tonne for U.S. hard red winter wheat.
"We (the U.S.) are way off base on that one," he said, referring to the higher U.S. wheat price.
